summary: Iteration 8 — Full backend+frontend regression for new subscription tiers (Solo £29.99 / Business £59.99 / Pro £99.99 / Enterprise £249.99), team management (invite/accept/role/remove), Enterprise contact-only checkout, white-label profile section, and accept-invite public route. 8/8 backend tests pass. All frontend acceptance criteria pass with one inconsistency found in role-update enterprise gating (admin-as-unlimited can INVITE manager but cannot PATCH manager).

minor.issue: Inconsistency: admin user (isUnlimited=True) effective_plan returns 'unlimited'. team_invite only blocks manager when plan=='pro', but team_update_role rejects unless plan=='enterprise'. So you can INVITE a manager but cannot LATER set someone to manager via PATCH — both endpoints should use the same gate. Suggest using a single helper `is_enterprise_or_unlimited(plan)` or treating 'unlimited' as enterprise in team_update_role.

issues: Searching 'Team' or 'Billing' in the sidebar search returns 'No tools match'. The sidebar filter uses `[...TOOLS, ...WOW_TOOLS]` (AppShell.jsx L26-27), but account-section tools (favourites, history, billing, team, profile, privacy, terms, complaints, refund, offline-mode) are returned as a HARD-CODED inline list inside `getToolsBySection('account')` (tools-config.js L695-708) and are NOT part of TOOLS/WOW_TOOLS. So they are invisible to the sidebar search. Recommend exporting an ACCOUNT_TOOLS array and including it in `allTools` in AppShell.jsx.

Account section is collapsed by default (openSections.account = false). Team Management link is only visible after expanding the section by scrolling to the bottom of the sidebar and clicking ACCOUNT. Consider opening it by default for admins with team-management entitlements, or pin the Team Management link near the top.

action_items: Unify enterprise-gating logic for the manager role between team_invite and team_update_role. Either accept 'unlimited' as enterprise in PATCH role, or block manager invites for non-enterprise too (current state allows the invite then blocks the assignment).

Expose account-section tools to the sidebar search filter (move inline list from getToolsBySection('account') into an exported ACCOUNT_TOOLS array, then include in `allTools` in AppShell.jsx so search picks them up).
Optional: default-open the Account section or surface Team Management higher in the sidebar so admins can find it without scrolling and expanding.
critical_code_review_comments: tools-config.js: account-section tools are duplicated as a hard-coded inline list inside getToolsBySection — duplicates the SECTIONS pattern and breaks the sidebar search. Recommend a single source of truth (ACCOUNT_TOOLS export).
server.py: team_update_role and team_invite use different plan checks for 'manager' role. Extract `def _can_use_manager_role(plan): return plan in ('enterprise','unlimited')` and reuse.
Backend tests created at /app/backend/tests/test_team_billing.py provide regression coverage for future iterations. Junit XML at /app/test_reports/pytest/iter8_team_billing.xml.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite is at /app/backend/tests/test_team_billing.py — run with `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest /app/backend/tests/test_team_billing.py -v`. The test for manager-role gating currently asserts the CURRENT (buggy-inconsistent) behaviour: PATCH manager on unlimited returns 400. If E1 fixes the inconsistency (treating unlimited as enterprise), flip that assertion to status_code == 200. Resend email send is MOCKED (falls back to mock logging when RESEND_API_KEY is empty) — invite emails won't actually send.
rca_of_the_issue: The manager-role gating inconsistency originates because `effective_plan(user)` returns 'unlimited' for isUnlimited admins (see billing.py), while server.py's `team_update_role` directly compares `plan != 'enterprise'` instead of using a helper. `team_invite` uses a different (looser) check `plan == 'pro'`. Reproduction: login as darrenhustle300 → POST /api/team/invite {role:'manager'} → succeeds. Then POST accept-invite → PATCH /api/team/members/{id} {role:'manager'} → 400 'The Manager role is only available on Enterprise plans.' Mitigation: introduce a single `_can_use_manager_role(plan)` helper used by both endpoints.
